claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells in response to TLR stimulation compared to healthy controls.

sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls.

claim_2.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed a significant reduction in the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells and decreased mTOR signaling as indicated by reduced pS6 expression.

sources.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts.
Additionally, there was reduced expression of pS6 [(phosphorylated ribosomal protein S6), a canonical target of mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) activation] in pDCs.

claim_3.claim: ELISA analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed increased levels of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and oncostatin M, which correlated with disease severity.

sources.quote: Given the pronounced and unappreciated observations of the enhanced plasma concentrations of TNFSF14, EN-RAGE, and OSM and their correlation to disease severity, we used an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to independently validate these results.

claim_4.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed an early but transient induction of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15, despite impaired type I IFN production.

sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15.
